calls.head: Depth against star power
calls.body: On depth, Utah is the league’s best, but New Jersey is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Mammoth.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Mammoth take down the Devils
paras: The Devils’ Jesper Boqvist played his first game of the season, after missing the first two. Clayton Keller struck first for the Mammoth on the power play just under two minutes in. Luke Evangelista scored his first goal for New Jersey on the power play midway through the first to tie it 1-1. It was a busy second period. MacKenzie Weegar put the Mammoth ahead 2-1 early in the period, with Mikhail Sergachev picking up his 300th NHL assist on the assist. Evangelista scored his second of the night less than five minutes later to tie it 2-2. Nick Schmaltz put the Mammoth ahead for good on the power play midway through the second, his fourth straight game with a goal. Lawson Crouse made it 4-2 late in the period, and that goal turned out to be the winner. Brenden Dillon and Jack McBain fought early in the third. Boqvist cut Utah’s lead to 4-3 midway through the period, but they got no closer. Vincent Trocheck scored his first goal for Utah with just over three minutes left to make it 5-3 for the Mammoth. There were two three-point nights: Schmaltz with a goal and two assists, and Sergachev with three assists.
The Mammoth had the better of the chances. Karel Vejmelka made 30 saves for the Mammoth, and Jake Allen stopped 26 of 31.
Weegar took three penalties on his own. The Mammoth improved to 3-1-0, and the Devils dropped to 1-2-0.

items.text: Jesper Bratt tied Kirk Muller for fourth on the Devils’ all-time scoring list, with 520 points.
Both of the preview’s calls held.
